story.originalTitle: How driver talent still makes a big difference under F1 2026 rules
story.summaryEn: Amid much criticism from drivers about the heavy-handed intervention of software in their control of the car, last year's constructors' championship-winning team says talent still counts. A tweak to the regulations ahead of the Miami Grand Prix reduced some of the criticised 'yo-yo racing', but more recently speed differences caused by the power units' self-learning algorithms have caused a great deal of angst.
detailZh: 在F1 2026规则下，车手天赋如何仍能产生巨大差异
在车手们对软件对其赛车控制进行粗暴干预提出大量批评之际，去年的车队总冠军车队表示，天赋依然重要
乔治·拉塞尔，梅赛德斯；奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里，迈凯伦
自F1赛季开始前，抱怨就一直没有停过。这些抱怨会周期性地加剧，尤其是在所谓的“能量匮乏”赛道上，那里的弯道与直道比例以及弯道类型不利于新一代赛车在单圈中为电池充电。
迈阿密大奖赛前实施的一项规则微调，减少了部分因车手处于不同电量状态而备受批评的“溜溜球式比赛”。但最近，动力单元的自学习算法对赛道条件和驾驶技术的微小变化做出反应，由此导致的速度差异引发了大量焦虑。
在斯帕，奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里将其描述为“一种相当糟糕的赛车方式”。
但情况在短期内不会改变，尽管有人主张完全禁止机器学习工具——通常引用F1运动规则中的一句话作为终结语。B1.9.1条规定：“车手必须独自且无辅助地驾驶赛车”。
而且仍有理由认为，最好的车手将能应对这些新挑战，尽管它们可能既晦涩又烦人。这是迈凯伦工程总监尼尔·霍尔迪在F1夏休期举行的一次圆桌采访中表达的观点。
当被Autosport问及目前是否能准确评估车手表现时，他说：“实际上，那些明白自己需要做什么的车手，那些头脑清醒的车手，那些世界上最好的F1车手，仍然会是最快的。”
“可能变化在于……这不再完全关乎最高速度，而是关乎背后产生那个圈速的思维过程。”
“斯帕就是一个很好的例子，实际上奥斯卡确实采用了略有不同的能量部署计划，这意味着他损失了零点几秒，但仍能与兰多持平。但我认为这些事情最终会平衡。你仍然能在总圈速以及比赛中看到好车手与不那么好的车手之间的差距。”
“我的回答真的是，最终一切都会扯平。可能某场比赛或某节排位赛会对某位车手或另一位不利，但我仍然认为，到赛季结束时，你会看到最好的车手出现在最好的位置上。”
卫冕冠军兰多·诺里斯在匈牙利赢得了今年首个大奖赛胜利。
从根本上说，当前规则集的局限性——电能部署与内燃机动力接近50:50的分配——在于赛车能储存的能量总量。由于电池必须在整个单圈中充电，出于安全和性能原因，软件干预是必要的，以逐渐减少电能部署，而不是让它突然耗尽。
机器学习软件还具有性能功能，它构成了工程师们建立“最优圈”尝试的一部分——“最优圈”是收获与部署的组合，能给出最快圈速。迈阿密规则调整的效果是让FIA有更大余地降低能量回收限制，以牺牲峰值速度换取更持续（尽管略低）的最高速度。
但所有这些都要求车手在控制输入（如油门位置）上保持一致。例如，如果他们入弯过于激进，在同一位置比队友损失更多速度，重新加速会消耗电能，因此他们会在单圈后段因可用能量减少而受到惩罚。
Houldey认为，这与车手习惯的风险与回报顺序不同：如今激进驾驶带来的回报少于更理性、更自律的驾驶方式。
“这绝对更像是一场脑力游戏，”他说，“而且车手需要处理的事情肯定比以前多得多——即便是2022-25年（地面效应时代），车手也有很多事情要做。但现在又多了一层，你不仅要把弯道速度做对，还必须把能量部署方式、油门位置等所有细节都做到绝对正确。”
“对工程团队来说，要从这些赛车中挖掘最大潜力，技术挑战肯定更大；对车手来说，要从这些赛车中挖掘最大潜力，技术挑战也更大。而最终，一如既往，赛车、车手和工程团队的最佳组合会做得最好。”
detailEn: How driver talent still makes a big difference under F1 2026 rules
Amid much criticism from the drivers about the heavy-handed intervention of software in their control of the car, last year’s constructors’ championship-winning team says talent still counts
George Russell, Mercedes, Oscar Piastri, McLaren

The complaints have been rumbling since before the start of the Formula 1 season. Periodically they intensify, especially at so-called ‘energy-starved’ circuits where the ratio of corners to straights, and the type of corners, mitigate against the new-generation cars being able to recharge their batteries through the lap.

A tweak to the regulations implemented ahead of the Miami Grand Prix reduced some of the much-criticised ‘yo-yo racing’ caused by drivers being in different states of charge. But more recently speed differences caused by the power units’ self-learning algorithms reacting to small variations in track conditions and driving technique have caused a great deal of angst.
In Spa, Oscar Piastri described it as a "pretty crap way of going racing".

But the situation isn’t going to change in the immediate future, even though there are those who argue in favour of the machine-learning tools being banned entirely – usually citing a phrase from F1’s sporting regulations as a mic drop. Section B1.9.1 states: "The driver must drive the car alone and unaided".

And there is still an argument to state that the best drivers will manage these new challenges, abstruse and bothersome though they may be. That was the perspective of McLaren’s technical director for engineering Neil Houldey in a round-table interview conducted during F1’s summer break.

"Actually the drivers who understand what they need to do, the ones who are switched on, the ones who are the best F1 drivers in the world are the ones who are still going to be the fastest," he said when asked by Autosport if it’s currently possible to assess driver performance accurately.
"It may have changed in terms of… It's not all about top speed, it's about the thought processes going on in the background that generate that lap time.

"[Spa] is a good example where actually Oscar did get a slightly different deployment schedule, which meant he lost a couple of tenths, but was up with Lando. But I think those things balance out. You still see the difference between the good drivers and the less good drivers in the overall lap time and then in the race as well.

"My answer really would be that it all evens out in the end. That there might be a race or a qualifying session here or there where that disadvantages one driver or the other, but I still think you see the best drivers come out in the best place at the end of the season."
Defending champion Lando Norris took his first GP win of the year in Hungary

Fundamentally the limitation of the current ruleset, with its near-50:50 split of electrical deployment to internal combustion power, is the amount of energy the car can store. Since the battery has to be recharged throughout the lap, software intervention is required for safety as well as performance reasons, to taper the electrical deployment rather than have it run out suddenly.

The machine-learning software also has a performance function in that it forms part of the engineers’ attempts to establish the "optimal lap" – the combinations of harvesting and deployment which gives the fastest lap time. The effect of the Miami rule tweaks, which gave the FIA more leeway to reduce energy harvesting limits, was to trade off peak speeds against a more sustained (if slightly lower) top speed.

But all this requires the driver to be consistent with the control inputs such as throttle position. If they attack a corner too aggressively and scrub off more speed than their team-mate in the same place, for instance, re-accelerating costs electrical power so they are punished by having less available later in the lap.
Houldey views it as a different order of risk and reward than drivers are used to: aggression now carries fewer rewards than a more cerebral and disciplined approach.

"It's definitely more of a thinking game," he said. "And there's definitely a lot more going on for the drivers than there was – even 2022-25 [the ground-effect era] there was a lot happening for the drivers to be doing. But now it's that extra bit, and you've got to get not only your cornering speeds right, but you've got to get the way you go about deploying your energy, your throttle position, whatever it might be, absolutely right as well.

"It's certainly more technically challenging for the engineering team to get the most out of these cars, and it's more technically challenging for the drivers to get the most out of these cars. And in the end, as always, the best combination of car, driver, engineering team ends up doing the best job."

relatedItems.originalTitle: Christian Horner proposes major change to how fans watch F1
relatedItems.summaryEn: Former Red Bull Racing CEO and team principal Christian Horner has suggested that Formula 1 should let fans sit virtually on their favourite team's pitwall and hear how strategy calls are made.
detailZh: 克里斯蒂安·霍纳建议对F1车迷的观赛方式做出重大改变
克里斯蒂安·霍纳建议让F1车迷以虚拟方式进入车队指挥台（pitwall），从而更深入地了解比赛策略与决策过程
赛道之外的赛车文化。车手生活方式、时尚、旅行、设计，以及那些让赛车超越运动本身的故事。
前红牛车队首席执行官兼领队克里斯蒂安·霍纳主张，F1应允许车迷以虚拟方式坐进自己支持车队的指挥台（pitwall），听到策略决定是如何做出的。
霍纳在2025年7月离开红牛后，在过去15个月里以车迷身份观看大奖赛，这是他职业生涯中的第一次。
周三在纽约举行的汽车运动商业交流会上发言时，这位英国人表示，维修区指挥台所知与电视观众所见之间的差距令他感到惊讶。
汽车运动商业交流会在纽约市迎来第二届，汇聚了来自赛车运动、商业和品牌领域的高层领袖，地点设在曼哈顿汽车展厅，共同探讨赛车运动在美国的发展。
克里斯蒂安·霍纳自离开甲骨文红牛车队以来首次在美国出席该活动。
其他小组成员还包括七届纳斯卡杯系列赛冠军吉米·约翰逊、前一级方程式董事长兼首席执行官蔡斯·凯里、通用汽车的马克·罗伊斯、潘世奇的乔纳森·吉布森以及纳斯卡的蒂姆·克拉克。
“但对我来说，这也是一种不同的视角。作为一名车迷、一名观众，突然听着我25年都没听过的解说员解说比赛，突然感觉……从维修区墙上那个充满各种信息、知识、策略和对手分析等的茧房里，突然之间你只有屏幕，解说员在解释发生了什么，还有不同的图形，”他说。
“感觉他们本可以揭开更多内幕。车队对此抵制，因为他们不想泄露知识产权和竞争优势。但看看现在观众消费的方式，以及他们对数据和信息的渴望与热切，从我坐在维修区墙上的经历突然变成一名观众，对手分析和策略以及比赛走势的呈现、还有沟通交流，可获取的内容之多令人惊叹。
红牛车队成员在维修区墙上
"显然，这些都在指挥台（pitwall）上进行等等。所以我真的觉得这是一个可以进一步开发的领域，让观众获得更好的体验。"
当被问及如何为车迷实现这一点时，霍纳补充道："也许可以做成互动式的。为什么不虚拟地坐在你最喜欢的车队的指挥台上，了解他们是如何做出决定的、他们正在进行哪些讨论。
"现在，作为一支车队，我会反对这样做，因为你不想把那些信息泄露出去。但归根结底，体育就是娱乐，现在竞争如此激烈，一级方程式已经把自己带到了这个不可思议的位置，当然是通过Netflix系列剧，我们拥有了这一整代新的车迷和不同类型的车迷。
"它必须不断进化。它不能停滞不前，而且它现在处于如此好的位置。它不能原地踏步，我相信它不会，但你必须不断进化。"
detailEn: Christian Horner proposes major change to how fans watch F1
Christian Horner has suggested giving F1 fans virtual access to team pitwalls to offer greater insight into race strategies and decision-making
Motorsport culture beyond the track. Driver lifestyle, fashion, travel, design and the stories that make racing more than a sport.
Former Red Bull Racing CEO and team principal Christian Horner argued that Formula 1 should let fans sit on their favourite team's pitwall virtually and hear how strategy calls are made.
Horner has spent the past 15 months watching grands prix as a fan for the first time in his career, after leaving Red Bull in July 2025.
Speaking at the Autosport Business Exchange in New York on Wednesday, the Briton said the gap between what the pitwall knows and what TV viewers see had surprised him.

Autosport Business Exchange returned to New York City for its second edition, bringing together senior leaders from across motorsport, business and brands at the Manhattan Motorcars showroom to examine racing's growth in America
Christian Horner made his first U.S. appearance at the event since leaving Oracle Red Bull Racing

Other panellists included seven-time NASCAR Cup Series champion Jimmie Johnson, former chairman and CEO of Formula 1 Chase Carey, General Motors' Mark Reuss, Penske's Jonathan Gibson and NASCAR's Tim Clark

"But for me, it was also a different perspective. As a fan, as a spectator, suddenly watching races with commentators that I hadn't heard for 25 years and suddenly feeling... Going from that sort of cocoon on the pitwall with all that information and knowledge and strategies and competitor analysis and so on, suddenly you've just got the screen with the commentators explaining what's going on and different graphics," he said.

"It felt like there's so much more that they could lift the lid on. The teams fight against it because they don't want to give the IP away and a competitive advantage. But just looking at how viewers consume now and their hunger and eagerness for data and information, going from the experience that I had from sitting on the pitwall to suddenly being a viewer, it's amazing just how much more is available in terms of competitor analysis and strategy and how races are shaping up, and the communication.
Red Bull Racing team members on the pit wall
"Obviously, that's going on on the pitwall and so on. So I really feel that that's an area that could be further exploited to get the viewer an even better experience."

When asked how that could be done for fans, Horner added: "Maybe make it interactive. Why not sit on the pitwall, virtually, of your favourite team, understand how they're getting to the decisions that they are, the discussions that they're having.

"Now, as a team, I would have argued against that because you don't want to be giving that information away. But, at the end of the day, sport is entertainment and there's so much competition now that Formula 1 has got itself into this incredible place where, certainly through the Netflix series, we've got this whole new generation and variants of fans.
"It's got to keep evolving. It can't stagnate and it's in such a great spot. It can't stand still, which I'm sure it's not going to, but you've got to keep evolving."
keyPointsZh: 霍纳是在纽约举行的Autosport Business Exchange活动上发言时提出这一建议的

keyPointsEn: Horner made the suggestion while speaking at the Autosport Business Exchange in New York
He raised the idea as a way to give fans greater insight into race strategies and decision-making
